# Seed 0: final 100 epoch losses

Source: `lstm_training_history.csv`, `engine_disjoint_epoch_selection` stage, seed 0. Slopes are ordinary least-squares fits of loss against epoch; negative means declining loss.

| Window | Training slope per epoch | Validation slope per epoch | Validation start → end | Relative validation change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 581–600 (20) | -0.000082907 | -0.000163822 | 0.140109887 → 0.137448470 | -1.8995% |
| 551–600 (50) | -0.000073640 | -0.000116502 | 0.143343796 → 0.137448470 | -4.1127% |
| 501–600 (100) | -0.000072463 | -0.000119156 | 0.150250958 → 0.137448470 | -8.5207% |

Epoch 600 is the lowest validation loss of the run. Its improvement over the previous minimum (0.137813503 at epoch 598) is 0.000365033, greater than the frozen `min_delta = 0.0001`. The patience counter would therefore reset at epoch 600. The run ended because it hit `max_epochs = 600`; the observed training and validation trends have not flattened. This is practically non-converged under the frozen 600-epoch budget. It does not prove that unlimited training would continue to improve or that more epochs would change downstream endpoints.
